evidence.quote: description: 'Manage n8n credentials. Actions: list, get, create, update, delete, getSchema. Use getSchema to discover required fields before creating.

reason: Ordinary usage guidance: the word 'credentials' is the tool's subject (managing n8n credentials), and 'use getSchema first' serves the user's own request. No hidden steering, no data sent elsewhere.
fix: None for the description (see M004 for its annotation).

reason: This 0.0.0.0 default is only used to build the base URL shown by the unauthenticated info endpoint; it does not bind a socket.

Binding all interfaces is intended for container deployment; the MCP endpoints require a Bearer AUTH_TOKEN compared in constant time, the server refuses to start without a token and refuses the default token in production. Remaining gaps on GET/DELETE /mcp are covered in M003.
fix: Optionally default HOST to 127.0.0.1 outside Docker.

reason: Same as F002: only used to display the base URL in the info response.

POST /mcp in the legacy server requires a Bearer token checked with a timing-safe compare; the bind address alone is not an exposure. Note this legacy server only warns (does not refuse) when the default AUTH_TOKEN is used.
fix: Refuse to start with the default AUTH_TOKEN in http-server.ts as the single-session server does.

title: POST /mcp logs every request's headers and full body at INFO, before authentication
reason: At the default LOG_LEVEL=info every request writes the Authorization bearer token, the x-n8n-key tenant API key, the mcp-session-id and the full JSON-RPC body (including credential data sent to n8n_manage_credentials create/update) to stdout/container logs, so anyone with log access gets the server token and tenants' n8n API keys.
fix: Drop the header/body dump or log only a redacted allowlist (method, path, content-length); never log Authorization, x-n8n-key or tools/call arguments. Do the same for the POST /mcp/test handler (line 1027).

title: Per-request x-n8n-url is checked once but redirects and later DNS answers are not
reason: An authenticated caller sets x-n8n-url; the check resolves DNS once, but the axios client re-resolves on every call (DNS rebinding) and follows redirects by default, so a host that passes the check and then 302-redirects (or re-resolves) to 169.254.169.254 or an internal service is reached with the n8n API client, and responses come back to the caller. The IPv6 check also only matches the literal prefixes fc00:/fd00: (other fc00::/7 addresses pass).
fix: Pin the validated IP for the connection (custom lookup/http agent), set maxRedirects: 0 on the n8n API and webhook axios clients (or re-validate each hop), and test IPv6 ranges with a real CIDR check; only accept x-n8n-url when ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT=true.

title: GET and DELETE /mcp skip the Bearer check and rely on the session ID alone

evidence.quote: app.delete('/mcp', async (req: express.Request, res: express.Response): Promise<void> => {

reason: Anyone who learns a session ID (they are logged, see M001) can attach to that session's server-to-client stream or terminate it without the AUTH_TOKEN. Session IDs are random UUIDs, so this needs a leak first.
fix: Call this.authenticateRequest(req, res) at the top of GET /mcp (session branch) and DELETE /mcp.

title: Credential tool that can delete/overwrite secrets is annotated non-destructive
reason: n8n_manage_credentials supports delete and update but declares destructiveHint: false, so clients that auto-approve non-destructive tools will let a prompt-injected agent delete or replace n8n credentials without asking.
fix: Set destructiveHint: true (or split delete/update into a separate destructive tool) and require confirmation for credential changes.
